**Early beta.** This is the first test build of JConnect for Windows. Expect rough edges, and don't rely on it as your only way into a computer yet.

## Download

- **JConnect-Setup-0.1.0-beta.1.exe**: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit, 91 MB
- SHA-256: `b4b5eb13a4c984ed0fb925eed86903ad8c7bd195b09fdd7c4e0b7bce534c76e1`

It's the same installer the JConnect website offers. It installs JConnect for your user account without admin rights and adds Start menu and desktop shortcuts.

JConnect isn't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Choose **More info → Run anyway**. When Windows Firewall asks, allow JConnect on private networks so your other devices can reach this computer.

## What's in this beta

- Remote desktop between your computers: nearby computers show up on their own. Pair once with a 6-digit code, then press **Connect**.
- End-to-end encryption on every connection, with Ed25519 device identities, X25519 key exchange and XSalsa20-Poly1305.
- JVPN, JConnect's built-in network, alongside Tailscale, Twingate, ZeroTier, WireGuard and Windows VPN connections. JConnect can import the machines they already know.
- An optional account with end-to-end encrypted sync and two-step sign-in.
- An SSH terminal, Remote Desktop (RDP) files, desktop shortcuts and Wake-on-LAN.
- Travel Mode, Emergency Lockdown, trusted devices and owner controls.
- Use a computer from a phone, tablet or TV browser on the same network by scanning a QR code.

## Known limits

- Windows only for now. A macOS version is on the way.
- Accounts, sync and JVPN away from home need a JConnect Cloud server that you run yourself. There's no hosted service yet.
- Windows can't be controlled on the secure desktop: UAC prompts, Ctrl+Alt+Del and the lock screen.
- There are no automatic updates yet. Download new betas from the Releases page.
